meta.source: Spider (Yu et al., 2018) train-split questions + official gold SQL (combined_data.parquet), verbatim -- third-party authored, not hand-written for this project.
meta.purpose: Held-out evaluation domain: a Spider database no system, prompt or engine fix was developed on. Built mechanically by heldout/build_domains.py under the rule fixed in heldout/PREREGISTRATION.md before any held-out cell ran.
meta.selection_note: 23 Spider questions covering 23 distinct gold queries, deduplicated by exact gold SQL text (first phrasing kept). Every distinct query kept; none authored, reworded, dropped or padded.
meta.register_rule: the table the most deduplicated questions read alone, ties to more rows then name: {'station': 12, 'train': 3, 'train_station': 0}
meta.tiers: Mechanical (heldout/sql_tier.py): out_of_scope_register if the gold SQL reads any table other than the register; else out_of_contract_aggregate if it uses a construct outside the Goal vocabulary (architectural_gap lists each); else the SQL structure (filter/aggregate/group_by/order_by), the answer tier.
meta.tier_convention_note: As in the released Spider corpora: out_of_scope_register questions are answerable in principle but need a table outside the register (expected_behavior=refuse); out_of_contract_aggregate questions are in scope by tau and excluded from scoring because the Goal vocabulary cannot express them (expected_behavior=answer, gold executed).

queries.question: How many train stations are there?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM station

queries.question: Show the name, location, and number of platforms for all stations.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT name ,  LOCATION ,  number_of_platforms FROM station

queries.question: What are all locations of train stations?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT LOCATION FROM station

queries.question: Show the names and total passengers for all train stations not in London.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT name ,  total_passengers FROM station WHERE LOCATION != 'London'

queries.question: Show the names and main services for train stations that have the top three total number of passengers.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT name ,  main_services FROM station ORDER BY total_passengers DESC LIMIT 3

queries.question: What is the average and maximum number of total passengers for train stations in London or Glasgow?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT avg(total_passengers) ,  max(total_passengers) FROM station WHERE LOCATION  =  'London' OR LOCATION  =  'Glasgow'

queries.question: Show all locations and the total number of platforms and passengers for all train stations in each location.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT LOCATION ,  sum(number_of_platforms) ,  sum(total_passengers) FROM station GROUP BY LOCATION

queries.question: Show all locations that have train stations with at least 15 platforms and train stations with more than 25 total passengers.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT LOCATION FROM station WHERE number_of_platforms  >=  15 AND total_passengers  >  25

queries.question: Show all locations which don't have a train station with at least 15 platforms.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT LOCATION FROM station EXCEPT SELECT LOCATION FROM station WHERE number_of_platforms  >=  15

queries.question: Show the location with most number of train stations.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT LOCATION FROM station GROUP BY LOCATION ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1
